brief: Goldman TMT sales note on Friday 25 Sep flows and the AI-infrastructure capex debate. Oracle issued a force majeure notice to the Blue Owl-backed developer of its Project Jupiter New Mexico data center; the desk reads this as legal protection against paying rent before the site is operational, not an exit, but says it signals rising execution risk (permitting, power, community opposition) in hyperscale AI builds and shows third-party AI infrastructure is not the bond-like asset it can appear to be. Separately, Anthropic signed an $11.6bn, seven-year Akamai CPU-capacity deal, expandable by $9bn to roughly $20bn total, about six times its May contract, carrying $5.5bn of capex plus $1.7bn of extra 2026 supply-chain spend; the desk reads this as frontier-model demand spreading beyond GPUs. Two GIR pieces argue the debate is shifting from spending size to required returns: hyperscalers need about $1.42tn of cumulative AI revenue in 2028-30 (about $11.6bn per GW per year) for 15% ROIC on 2026-27 AI capex, or per Portfolio Strategy about $300bn of annual AI revenue plus up to $1tn of app spend; realized hyperscaler ROIC has fallen from 40% to 25%. Conclusion: the AI trade stays supported, but future returns should come from selective winners, not broad capex exposure.
